simple.meaning: מָרָק (mârâq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “soup (as if a rinsing ).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Judges, Isaiah, beginning at Judges 6:19. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָרָק (H4839).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מָרָק (mârâq) / H4839 is traced through Judges 6:19, Judges 6:20, Isaiah 65:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes of an ephah † 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel of meal. He put the meat in a basket and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out to him under the oak, and presented it.

definitions.full: H4839. maraq מָרָק (van d. H מָרַק ) noun masculine juice stewed out of meat, or broth (on form compare Lag BN 50 ); — בַּמָּרוּר שָׂם וְהַמָּרָק Judg 6:19 (see GFM); שְׁפוֺךְ וְאֶתהַֿמָּרָק 6:20 ; construct מְרַק Isa 65:4 Qr, so Vrss (Kt פרק ) broth of unclean things. [ מֶרְקָח ], מִרְקַ֫תַת מֶרְקָחָה, see רקח .
